lang|es}}.][https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=008985 Bolmaro, Leandro – Nationality: Italy.] professional [[basketball]] player for [[Olimpia Milano]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He also represents the senior [[Argentina men's national basketball team|Argentina national team]].{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=NBA mock draft: What would the likely lottery teams do at No. 1? |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/insider/story/_/id/28453206/nba-mock-draft-likely-lottery-teams-do-no-1 |website=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=11 January 2020 |date=10 January 2020}} ==Early years and youth career== Bolmaro began playing the sport of basketball in his home country of Argentina. He started playing with the youth teams of a local [[sports club]] named Almafuerte from [[:es:Las Varillas|Las Varillas]] town in [[Córdoba Province, Argentina|Córdoba]]. On 13 April 2018, he played for the World Team at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] in [[Portland, Oregon]].{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=World Team roster announced for Nike Hoop Summit |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nba/post/_/id/32598/world-team-roster-announced-for-nike-hoop-summit |website=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=11 January 2020 |date=6 April 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Estudiantes de Bahía Blanca (2017–2018)=== Bolmaro began his pro career on 16 July 2017, when he was 16 years old, after he signed with [[Estudiantes de Bahía Blanca]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Básquet]], the top basketball league in Argentina.{{cite web |title=Bahía sumó dos chicos de enorme proyección: Lugarini y Bolmaro|url=https://basquetplus.com/articulo/bahía-sumó-dos-chicos-de-enorme-proyección-lugarini-y-bolmaro|website=Básquet Plus|date=16 July 2017|accessdate=11 January 2020|language=Spanish }} In 23 games played during the [[2017–18 Liga Nacional de Básquet season|2017–18 season]], Bolmaro averaged 2.0 points, 0.7 rebounds, 0.5 assists, and 0.4 steals, in 7.2 minutes per game. He shot 37.3% overall from the field, 53.6% on 2-point field goals, 17.4% on 3-point field goals, and 75.0% on free throws.[https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=008985#!careerstats BOLMARO, LEANDRO Career Stats Other Competition.]{{cite web|last1=Castrejón|first1=Andrés|title=En Barcelona presumen de Leandro Bolmaro, su "Messi" del básquetbol|url=http://ar.marca.com/claro/basquetbol/2019/10/14/5da4e5dcca47414e488b4593.html|website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=Spanish|date=14 October 2019|accessdate=11 January 2020|archive-date=20 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220620064053/https://ar.marca.com/claro/basquetbol/2019/10/14/5da4e5dcca47414e488b4593.html|url-status=dead}} ===Barcelona (2018–2021)=== For the [[2018–19 LEB Oro season]], Bolmaro moved to the Spanish club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]]. He averaged 10.4 points, 3.1 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 1.2 steals per game for the club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet B|reserve team]] while playing in the [[Liga Española de Baloncesto|LEB Oro]], Spain's second-tier level league. With the reserve team, he played in a total of 33 games and averaged 24.1 minutes per game of playing time. He shot 39.6% overall from the field, 45.5% on 2-point field goals, 30.8% on 3-point field goals, and 65.2% on free throws.[http://competiciones.feb.es/estadisticas/Jugador.aspx?i=792134&c=2325541&med=0 BOLMARO, LEANDRO NICOLAS Temporada: 18/19 Equipo: BARÇA LASSA {{in lang|es}}.] In [[2019–20 FC Barcelona Bàsquet season]], he split playing time between Barcelona's reserve team and senior team, which competed in the [[Liga ACB]], the highest level Spanish league, and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|last1=Codocea|first1=Mauricio|title=La historia de Leandro Bolmaro, el otro argentino al que le dicen "Messi" en Barcelona|url=https://www.clarin.com/deportes/leandro-bolmaro-proceso_0_ZxdLRVr5.html |website=[[Clarín (Argentine newspaper)|Clarín]]|date=17 October 2019|accessdate=11 January 2020|language=Spanish}} During the [[2019–20 LEB Plata season|2019–20 Spanish 3rd Division]] season, while playing with Barcelona's reserve B team, he averaged 14.9 points, 2.7 rebounds, 3.6 assists, and 1.8 steals, in 26.3 minutes per game, in 9 games played in the [[LEB Plata|Spanish 3rd Division]]. On 13 August 2020, Bolmaro signed a contract extension with Barcelona through 2023.{{cite news|title=Barcelona signs Leandro Bolmaro to multi-year contract extension|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/barcelona-signs-leandro-bolmaro-to-multi-year-contract-extension/|website=Sportando|date=13 August 2020|accessdate=13 August 2020|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} After getting selected in the NBA draft, Bolmaro opted to stay with FC Barcelona.{{cite web|title=Leandro Bolmaro: 'It's time to repay Barça for their trust in me'|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1899986/leandro-bolmaro-its-time-to-repay-bara-for-their-trust-in-me |website=fcbarcelona.com|date=19 November 2020|accessdate=21 November 2020}} In September 2021, Bolmaro paid his [[buyout clause]] in order to leave Barcelona and subsequently be able to sign a 4-year rookie-scale contract with the Minnesota Timberwolves.{{cite web|url=https://www.gigantes.com/nba/leandro-bolmaro-nba/|publisher=Gigantes del Basket|title=Bolmaro se desvincula del Barça y aterriza en la NBA. Así será su nuevo contrato|website=Gigantes.com|date=15 September 2021|accessdate=15 September 2021|language=Spanish}}{{cite web|title=Agreement for the release of Leandro Bolmaro, The Argentine player has triggered his release clause|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/2256097/agreement-for-the-release-of-leandro-bolmaro|date=15 September 2021|website=fcbarcelona.com|accessdate=15 September 2021}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2021–2022)=== In the [[2020 NBA draft]], Bolmaro was selected by the [[New York Knicks]] with the 23rd overall selection,{{cite web|last1=Vega|first1=Julio|title=NBA draft 2020: Four things to know about Argentine prospect Leandro Bolmaro, taken No. 23 overall|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/draft/2020/11/18/leandro-bolmaro-nba-draft-new-york-knicks-trade/3766519001/|website=USA Today|date=18 November 2020|accessdate=21 November 2020}} but his draft rights were traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in a three-team trade.{{cite web|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Ricky Rubio And Draft Rights To Jaden McDaniels From Oklahoma City And Draft Rights To Leandro Bolmaro From New York|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-ricky-rubio-and-draft-rights-jaden-mcdaniels-oklahoma-city-and|website=NBA.com|date=20 November 2020|accessdate=21 November 2020}} On 18 September 2021, Bolmaro signed a 4-year, $11.8M rookie contract with the Timberwolves.{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Leandro Bolmaro|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-leandro-bolmaro|website=NBA.com|date=18 September 2021|access-date=19 September 2021}} Bolmaro made his NBA debut on 20 October 2021 in the Timberwolves 124–106 win against the [[Houston Rockets]]. He hadn't seen many minutes before 27 November 2021, in which he played a career-high 17 minutes against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. === Utah Jazz (2022–2023) === On 6 July 2022, Bolmaro was traded along with [[Malik Beasley]], [[Jarred Vanderbilt]], [[Patrick Beverley]], the draft rights to [[Walker Kessler]], four future first-round picks, and a pick swap to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Rudy Gobert]].{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Center Rudy Gobert from Utah Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-center-rudy-gobert-from-utah-jazz |access-date=2022-07-06 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} On 16 February 2023, Bolmaro reached a contract buyout agreement with the Jazz, and he was subsequently waived.{{cite web|title=Jazz Waive Leandro Bolmaro|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waive-leandro-bolmaro|date=February 16, 2023|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 16, 2023}} === Lenovo Tenerife (2023) === On 2 March 2023, Bolmaro signed with [[CB Canarias|Lenovo Tenerife]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web |title=EL LENOVO TENERIFE FICHA A LEANDRO BOLMARO |url=https://cbcanarias.net/2023/03/02/el-lenovo-tenerife-ficha-a-leandro-bolmaro/ |access-date=March 2, 2023 |website=CB Canarias}} === Bayern Munich (2023–2024) === On 19 July 2023 he signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1531012/leandro-bolmaro-signed-a-two-year-with-bayern/ |title=Leandro Bolmaro signed a two-year contract with Bayern |date=2023-07-19 |access-date=2024-06-22 |website=eurohoops.net}} On 6 July 2024, he opted out of his contract with the German club. ==National team career== ===Junior national team=== In 2017, Bolmaro won a silver medal with [[Argentina national under-17 basketball team|Argentina's Under-17 national team]] at the [[FIBA South America Under-17 Championship for Men|FIBA South America Under-17 Championship]] in [[Lima]], Peru. He averaged a team-high 13.8 points per game.{{cite web |title=Chile and Argentina will play for South American U17 Gold |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/sudamericano/u17/2017/news/chile-and-argentina-will-play-for-south-american-u17-gold |website=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=11 January 2020 |date=21 July 2017}} Bolmaro also represented the [[Argentina men's national under-19 basketball team|Argentine Under-19 national team]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece, where his team finished in 11th place. He left the tournament's opening game early with a minor strain.{{cite web |title=Barcelona's Bolmaro injured in FIBA U19 World Cup first day |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba/900680/barcelonas-bolmaro-injured-in-fiba-u19-world-cup-first-day/ |website=EuroHoops |accessdate=11 January 2020 |date=30 June 2019}} During the tournament, he was Argentina's leading scorer, with an average of 10.8 points per game. ===Senior national team=== On 29 July 2021, Bolmaro scored 2 points in a loss to the [[Spain men's national basketball team]] at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] in Tokyo, Japan. In 2022, Bolmaro won the gold medal with the senior team in the [[2022 FIBA AmeriCup]] held in [[Recife]], [[Brazil]].
